moments.label: M6.4 foreshock
moments.text: M6.4 at depth 10.5 km; USGS peak intensity MMI 8.4 (ComCat; 8.3 on the grid drawn here).

moments.label: M7.1 mainshock
moments.text: M7.1 about 34 hours later at depth 8 km; USGS peak intensity MMI 8.7 (ComCat; 8.6 on the grid drawn here).

moments.label: Largest aftershock M5.5
moments.text: The largest catalogued shock after the M7.1 was M5.5, 0.5 hours after it.

moments.label: One day after the M7.1
moments.text: 2232 shocks of M2 or more were catalogued in the first 24 hours after the M7.1 (the M7.1 itself not counted).

moments.label: One week after
moments.text: 3810 shocks of M2 or more in the first 7 days after the M7.1.

teaches.title: A few seconds can be enough
teaches.text: A few seconds of warning can be enough to begin drop, cover and hold on (it takes only a few seconds to start; see ShakeOut). Open the warning what-if and slide the delay: towns closest to the epicentre get none.
